    How to read this
    • A score is the expected number of large-animal carcass records (deer, moose, elk and other ungulates) on that segment in a year, from the 2021 to 2025 records.
    • Most of the ranking is exposure: about 90% of the top 5% of segments are in the top traffic decile. It shows where recorded collisions are likely, not where animals are most numerous.
    • Reporting differs about 25-fold between maintenance areas (1.9 to 47.1 records per 100 km a year), so compare segments inside one area. Use “Rank in area” or the area menu. A quiet area is not a safe one.
    • The Calgary and Edmonton ring roads (Highways 201 and 216) are over-predicted, 1.70 times their records together.
    • “Reliable areas” are the nine areas with at least 11 records per 100 km a year and a steady year-to-year level (504, 508, 509, 514, 516, 520, 521, 522, 524).
    • “With history” adds each segment's own records, which finds persistent hotspots but scores segments with no record down. A segment's own records mix real collisions with how well that stretch is recorded, and we cannot tell the two apart: read a big uplift over “Surroundings” as persistently high records, cause unconfirmed, and check the stretch before building. “Ungulates” adds predicted animal abundance; that gain was not confirmed on the fresh holdout.

    14,769 scored segments from risk_scores.csv and risk_scores_history.csv; lines simplified to about 40 m. Built by src/analysis/optional-make_risk_map.py.
